start.description:
Time starting from which available slots should be checked.
    
      Must be in UTC timezone as ISO 8601 datestring.
      
      You can pass date without hours which defaults to start of day or specify hours:
      2024-08-13 (will have hours 00:00:00 aka at very beginning of the date) or you can specify hours manually like 2024-08-13T09:00:00Z

end.description:
Time until which available slots should be checked.
      
      Must be in UTC timezone as ISO 8601 datestring.
      
      You can pass date without hours which defaults to end of day or specify hours:
      2024-08-20 (will have hours 23:59:59 aka at the very end of the date) or you can specify hours manually like 2024-08-20T18:00:00Z

timeZone.description: Time zone in which the available slots should be returned. Defaults to UTC.

duration.description: If event type has multiple possible durations then you can specify the desired duration here. Also, if you are fetching slots for a dynamic event then you can specify the duration her which defaults to 30, meaning that returned slots will be each 30 minutes long.

format.description: Format of slot times in response. Use 'range' to get start and end times.

bookingUidToReschedule.description: The unique identifier of the booking being rescheduled. When provided will ensure that the original booking time appears within the returned available slots when rescheduling.

rescheduleWithSameHost.description: Only for round robin event types that allow the person rescheduling to choose the host. True returns slots of the original host, false returns slots of any available host. Ignored for other event types.

queueResponse.description: Whether to queue the form response.

actions.name: create_event_type_sequence
actions.description: Create an event type sequence. Lets a booker book the team's event types back to back, as one loop. Every segment's event type must belong to the team and be bookable together: a 422 names each segment that isn't and why, and a slug already used by one of the team's sequences or event types is a 409. PBAC permission: `eventType.create`. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

matches.description: all: every condition matches; any: at least one matches; none: no conditions match; not_all: at least one condition does not match.

Zapier deliveries, custom payload templates that do not reference the field, the `AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` / `AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` bodies (delivered verbatim from the fire-time blob, never built) and the legacy `FORM_SUBMITTED_NO_EVENT` fallback delivery omit it.

customHeaders.description: Static HTTP headers sent on every webhook delivery (e.g. Authorization). Max 10 headers, values up to 4 KiB, stored encrypted and redacted on read. name.description: HTTP header name, at most 256 characters. Names starting with `X-Cal-` are reserved for Cal.com's own headers. Blocked names: host, content-length, transfer-encoding, connection, keep-alive, upgrade, trailer, te, proxy-authorization.

value.description: HTTP header value. Omit (or send the redacted `"***"`) on update to keep the stored value, as long as `subscriberUrl` stays the same: stored values are never sent to a new URL. Values are stored encrypted and are always redacted as `"***"` on read.

version.description: The payload format version of the webhook. Every version's builder-produced payload carries a `payload.platformOAuthClientId` field naming the owning platform OAuth client (`null` for non-platform events; for the flat-delivered MEETING_STARTED/MEETING_ENDED bodies the field appears at the top level of the body). Zapier deliveries, custom payload templates that do not reference the field, the `AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` / `AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` bodies (delivered verbatim from the fire-time blob, never built) and the legacy `FORM_SUBMITTED_NO_EVENT` fallback delivery omit it.

actions.name: create_booking
actions.description:
Create a booking. POST /v2/bookings is used to create regular bookings, recurring bookings and instant bookings. The request bodies for all 3 are almost the same except:
      If eventTypeId in the request body is id of a regular event, then regular booking is created.

      If it is an id of a recurring event type, then recurring booking is created.

      Meaning that the request bodies are equal but the outcome depends on what kind of event type it is with the goal of making it as seamless for developers as possible.

      For team event types it is possible to create instant meeting. To do that just pass `"instant": true` to the request body. If the event type has an instant meeting...

Send `true` when the booker ticked the opt-out and `false` when they were shown it and left it unticked. Sending `false` asserts that the booker saw the opt-out. Leave it out when the booker was not shown it: a booking without an answer is never looked up.

Must contain 2 to 20 distinct usernames, and can't be combined with eventTypeId, eventTypeSlug, username or teamSlug. Pass organizationSlug when the users belong to an organization; without it only users outside any organization are found. Platform managed users can only be booked with their own OAuth client's credentials or one of its access tokens; to any other request they are reported as not found. Duration defaults to 30 minutes and can be changed with lengthInMinutes (15, 30, 45, 60 or 90).

hostUsernames.description:
Only for collective event types: books just these hosts instead of every host. The organizer is whichever of them comes first in the event type's host order, not in this list. For a team in an organization, use the hosts' organization usernames. Fetch slots with the same hostUsernames first.

      Every username must be a host of the event type, otherwise the request fails with 400 and the message "invalid_hosts". At most 50 distinct usernames of at most 255 characters each. Leaving it out, or passing an empty list, books every host.

      Ignored for other event types and for dynamic group bookings (usernames). A seated or recurring collective event type refuses it with 400. Can't be sent with instant or recurrenceCount, and rescheduling a booking keeps the hosts of the original booking.

actions.name: get_discover_listings_by_id
actions.description: Get Discover listings by id. Returns published Discover listings by id, with the fields their public cards show: service name, provider, price, new-client discount, the provider's rating, review count and verification, duration, whether it is online, city, neighborhood and the business's time zone. With `includeNextAvailable`, also the earliest open slot in the next 7 days for the first 10 listings. Any id that is not a published listing is returned in `notFoundListingIds`. Requests with `includeNextAvailable` are limited to 60 per minute per user, shared across all of the user's API keys and access tokens. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_READ` scope is required.

ids.description: Discover listing ids, such as the `listingId` values a Discover search returned. Repeat the parameter (`ids=12&ids=34`) or separate the ids with commas (`ids=12,34`). Duplicates are read once.

includeNextAvailable.description: Also look up each listing's earliest open slot in the next 7 days. Only the first 10 listings are checked, so list the ones you care about first.

actions.name: search_discover_listings
actions.description: Search Discover listings. Searches the published Discover listings the way Cal.ai does. In-person results stay within the area you name, else around your saved ZIP code; with neither, nothing is searched and `areaNeeded` is returned. When the named area or the saved ZIP code cannot be found, nothing is searched and `areaNeeded` comes with `areaNotFound`. Online-only categories and `onlineOnly` searches are searched everywhere. An empty neighborhood widens to its whole region (`widenedFrom`); an empty search retries with the category alone (`broadenedFrom`); when the whole area has nothing, the web is searched there once and businesses not on Discover come back in `webBusinesses`. Availabi...

category.description: The Discover category the need maps to, such as `medical` for tooth pain.

subcategory.description: A subcategory of `category`, such as `dentistry` under `medical`. Ignored without its category, and named in `ignoredFilters` when it is not one of the category's.

query.description: Free text matched against the title, description, provider and subcategory. Never a place.

neighborhood.description: A neighborhood of a launch region, such as `Capitol Hill`, for in-person listings there only. An unknown name comes back in `ignoredFilters`.

onlineOnly.description: Keep only online listings and search them everywhere, whatever `area` says. Online searches never fall back to the web.

localQuery.description: For the web fallback, the need in the area's local language when it is not English, such as `Zahnarzt` for a dentist in Hamburg.

area.description: The place to search around: a ZIP code, neighborhood or city. Without it, the search uses your saved ZIP code, and answers `areaNeeded` when there is none. Pass `anywhere` for results from anywhere.

maximumPrice.description: The highest price, in whole currency units: 50 means $50, 0 means free only.

availableWithin.description: Only listings with a real open slot in this window, in your saved time zone. `this_week` means the next 7 days.

actions.name: call_web_found_business_to_book
actions.description: Call a web-found business to book. Has Cal's voice assistant call a business on the user's behalf to book the service, the way Cal.ai does once the user approves. Only a business that `GET /v2/discover/listings/search` returned in `webBusinesses` to this same user in the last 24 hours can be called, with its URL exactly as returned; a Discover listing is never called, because it is booked from its `bookingUrl`. Every check runs before the call: the account may place calls, the business's page offers a US or Canadian appointment phone, the name and service are plain words, the business was not called too recently, and the user's plan covers it. The call is placed by Cal's AI voice assistan...

businessUrl.description: The business's URL, exactly as a `search_listings` web business gave it in `webBusinesses[].url`. Only a business found by your own search in the last 24 hours can be called.

service.description: What to book, in plain words, such as `upright piano full tuning and pitch raise`. Put when the user can come in `timing`, the staff member they asked for in `staff` and their booking details in `notes`. Never put contact details (phone, email, address) in it.

timing.description: When the user can come, in their words, such as `Thursday after 5 or Friday morning`. Leave it out when they named no window. Never put contact details in it.

staff.description: The staff member the user asked for, in their words, such as `Sam`. Leave it out when they named none; never take one from the business's page.

notes.description: Booking details the user gave for this booking, such as `allergic to lavender`. Only what they said, never contact details. Leave it out when they gave none.

daysFromToday.description: The day the user asked for, in days from today in their saved time zone: 0 today, 1 tomorrow. Cal asks the business for that date. Leave it out when the user named no day.

callerName.description: The name the user gave for themselves, which Cal gives on the call. Leave it out to use the account name; never a name from a search result.

actions.name: book_web_found_business_online
actions.description: Book a web-found business online. Has Cal's booking agent book a service on a business's own online booking page for the user, the way Cal.ai does once the user approves. Only a business that `GET /v2/discover/listings/search` returned in `webBusinesses` to this same user in the last 24 hours can be booked, with its URL exactly as returned; a Discover listing is never booked this way, because it is booked from its `bookingUrl`. Every check runs before the job starts: the account may book online, has a username, has fewer than the allowed number of jobs running, and its plan covers the booking. The booking agent browses with AI, so a user in an organization that opted out of AI cannot book...

area.description: The user's area as they gave it: a ZIP code, neighborhood or city.

budgetDollars.description: The most the user wants to pay for the service, in US dollars, when they said so.

idempotencyKey.description: A key you generate once per booking, such as a UUID. Send the same key to retry the same request: you get its job back, and no second job starts.

actions.name: ask_to_be_told_when_discover_provider_joins
actions.description: Ask to be told when a Discover provider joins. Records that the authenticated user is looking for a service Discover has no listing for, so they are emailed at their account address when a matching provider joins. Asking again for the same need within 90 days returns the open request only in the same region: a repeat in another region, or with a `searchedArea` where there was none (or none where there was one), records a new request. `matchedProviders` in the response says which new providers can trigger the email: only online ones, or none, when the request is outside every launch region, so pass the `searchedArea` of the user's search. The response never includes the request's id, an em...

service.description: The service in two or three words, as a provider would list it, such as dentist or piano lessons. Never the user's own words or personal details.

category.description: The Discover category it belongs to.

subcategory.description: The subcategory slug within that category, when one fits. A subcategory outside the category is ignored.

searchedArea.description: The `searchedArea` a `search_listings` (`GET /v2/discover/listings/search`) result returned when it found nothing, copied as given; it decides the region the request is matched in, and a repeat returns the open request only from the same region. Leave it out when there was none.

actions.name: get_sequence_s_booking_page
actions.description: Get a sequence's booking page. What a booker sees before booking the sequence: its segments in order, who each collective segment is with, and the questions asked once for the whole sequence. No authentication is required. A sequence that can't be booked right now is not found.

actions.name: get_sequence_s_available_start_times
actions.description: Get a sequence's available start times. The times at which the whole sequence can be booked: every segment fits its own hosts, notice and booking window, back to back. Each start time is when the first segment begins. No authentication is required, and each caller can make 60 requests a minute. A sequence that can't be booked right now returns no start times.

start.description:
Time starting from which available slots should be checked.
    
      Must be in UTC timezone as ISO 8601 datestring.
      
      You can pass date without hours which defaults to start of day or specify hours:
      2024-08-13 (will have hours 00:00:00 aka at very beginning of the date) or you can specify hours manually like 2024-08-13T09:00:00Z

end.description:
Time until which available slots should be checked.
      
      Must be in UTC timezone as ISO 8601 datestring.
      
      You can pass date without hours which defaults to end of day or specify hours:
      2024-08-20 (will have hours 23:59:59 aka at the very end of the date) or you can specify hours manually like 2024-08-20T18:00:00Z

timeZone.description: Time zone in which the available slots should be returned. Defaults to UTC.

actions.name: get_event_type_calendar_invite_templates
actions.description: Get event-type calendar-invite templates. Returns host and guest invite-description settings resolved from the event type, organization default when the mode is `inherit`, then Cal.com's standard description. Access matches reading the event type; OAuth clients require `EVENT_TYPE_READ`. Custom templates are limited to 5,000 characters. Managed children inherit their parent's templates and are marked read-only. Host templates are private and are not included in event-type responses.

actions.name: update_event_type_calendar_invite_templates
actions.description: Update event-type calendar-invite templates. Updates host and/or guest settings without changing other event-type fields; omitted audiences remain unchanged. `inherit` uses the organization default, `standard` uses Cal.com's standard description, and `custom` uses a supplied template of at most 5,000 characters. HTML tags are stripped and Markdown links are kept. Managed children are read-only and return HTTP 400; update their parent. Access matches updating the event type; OAuth clients require `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE`.

Create an event type. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section.</Note>

If `bookingFields` is omitted, the event type is created with its default booking fields. At least one contact field—`email` or `attendeePhoneNumber`—must remain visible and required. Other default fields, such as additional notes, can be hidden. Provide `bookingFields` to customize the default fields or add custom booking fields. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

rolling.description:
Determines the behavior of the booking window:
      - If **true**, the window is rolling. This means the number of available days will always be equal the specified 'value' 
        and adjust dynamically as bookings are made. For example, if 'value' is 3 and availability is only on Mondays, 
        a booker attempting to schedule on November 10 will see slots on November 11, 18, and 25. As one of these days 
        becomes fully booked, a new day (e.g., December 2) will open up to ensure 3 available days are always visible.
        In this mode 'value' must be at most 61, because availability is only searched up to 61 days ahead.
      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the
        moment someone is trying to book. For example, if 'value' is 3, availability is only on Mondays, and the current 
        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

actions.name: list_event_types
actions.description:
List event types. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Hidden event types and hidden booking fields are returned only when listing your own event types. Other callers see public event types and visible booking fields.

username.description: The username of the user to get event types for. If only username provided will get all event types.

eventSlug.description: Slug of event type to return. Notably, if eventSlug is provided then username must be provided too, because multiple users can have event with same slug.

usernames.description: Get dynamic event type for multiple usernames separated by comma. e.g `usernames=alice,bob`

orgSlug.description: slug of the user's organization if he is in one, orgId is not required if using this parameter

orgId.description: ID of the organization of the user you want the get the event-types of, orgSlug is not needed when using this parameter

sortCreatedAt.description: Sort event types by creation date. When not provided, no explicit ordering is applied.

actions.name: get_event_type_history
actions.description:
Get event type history. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_READ` scope is required.

Only the event type owner and applicable administrators can view its history. General event type read access does not include access to its history.

limit.description: The number of audit logs to return. Defaults to 25 and cannot exceed 50.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous response. Pass `pagination.nextCursor` to fetch the next page of audit logs.

actions.name: get_scheduling_configuration
actions.description:
Get scheduling configuration. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

The response varies by the event type's scheduling type, and non-team event types are rejected.

If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_READ` scope is required.

actions.name: list_crm_sync_errors_for_event_type
actions.description:
List CRM sync errors for an event type. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

By default, only active CRM sync errors are returned; pass `includeDismissed=true` to include dismissed errors.

If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_READ` scope is required.

appSlug.description: CRM app slug connected to the event type, for example `salesforce`.

includeDismissed.description: When true, returns dismissed historical errors as well as active errors. Defaults to false.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from `pagination.nextCursor`. Omit to fetch the first page of CRM sync errors.

limit.description: Maximum number of CRM sync errors to return.

actions.name: get_event_type
actions.description:
Get an event type. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Returns hidden booking fields only to callers who are allowed to view them. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_READ` scope is required.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

actions.name: update_event_type
actions.description:
Update an event type. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Omit `bookingFields` to keep the existing booking fields. If provided, the array replaces them, and any omitted default fields are restored with their default settings. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

mode.description: Template source. `inherit` uses the organization default, `standard` uses Cal.com's standard description, and `custom` uses this object's template.

slotInterval.description:
Number representing length of each slot when event is booked. By default it equal length of the event type.
      If event length is 60 minutes then we would have slots 9AM, 10AM, 11AM etc. but if it was changed to 30 minutes then
      we would have slots 9AM, 9:30AM, 10AM, 10:30AM etc. as the available times to book the 60 minute event.

bookingWindow.description: Limit how far in the future this event can be booked

type.description: Whether the window should be business days, calendar days or a range of dates

value.description: How many business day into the future can this event be booked

rolling.description:
Determines the behavior of the booking window:
      - If **true**, the window is rolling. This means the number of available days will always be equal the specified 'value' 
        and adjust dynamically as bookings are made. For example, if 'value' is 3 and availability is only on Mondays, 
        a booker attempting to schedule on November 10 will see slots on November 11, 18, and 25. As one of these days 
        becomes fully booked, a new day (e.g., December 2) will open up to ensure 3 available days are always visible.
        In this mode 'value' must be at most 61, because availability is only searched up to 61 days ahead.
      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the
        moment someone is trying to book. For example, if 'value' is 3, availability is only on Mondays, and the current 
        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

value.description: How many calendar days into the future can this event be booked

        In this mode 'value' must be at most 61, because availability is only searched up to 61 days ahead.
      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the

        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

hideTranscriptionForGuests.description: If true, guests will not see live transcription captions during the meeting

hideTranscriptionForOrganizer.description: If true, organizers will not see live transcription captions during the meeting

sendTranscriptionEmails.description: Send emails with the transcription of the Cal Video after the meeting ends.

disableAttendeeRecordingDownloadEmail.description: If true, attendees will not receive the Cal Video recording download email for this event type. Defaults to false. Organization guest notifications can still prevent this email from sending.

transcriptionLanguage.description: Deepgram language code for transcription (e.g. 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'pt-BR', or 'multi' for auto-detect). Defaults to English when not set.

calVideoSettings.description: Cal video settings for the event type

bookingRequiresAuthentication.description: Boolean to require authentication for booking this event type via api. If true, only authenticated users who are the event-type owner or org/team admin/owner can book this event type.

disabled.description: If true, cancelling is always disabled for this event type.

disableCancelling.description: Settings for disabling cancelling of this event type.

disabled.description: If true, rescheduling is always disabled for this event type.

minutesBefore.description: Disable rescheduling when less than the specified number of minutes before the meeting. If set, `disabled` should be false or undefined.

disableRescheduling.description: Settings for disabling rescheduling of this event type. Can be always disabled or disabled when less than X minutes before the meeting.

interfaceLanguage.description: Set preferred language for the booking interface. Use empty string for visitor's browser language (default).

weekStart.description: Day the booking page calendar starts the week on. Overrides the host's account setting for this event type only. Omit or set to null to inherit the account setting.

allowReschedulingPastBookings.description: Enabling this option allows for past events to be rescheduled.

allowReschedulingCancelledBookings.description: When enabled, users will be able to create a new booking when trying to reschedule a cancelled booking.

showOptimizedSlots.description: Arrange time slots to optimize availability.

useIsolatedAvailability.description: When true, only this event type's own Cal.com bookings block the slot. The availability schedule and connected calendars still apply. Same as "Consider only this booking link's bookings" in the web app. Requires an organization with at least 15 members.

privateNoteEnabled.description: When enabled, a private note calendar event is created alongside the booking with the resolved template as its description. Only visible to the host.

privateNoteMode.description: How private notes are delivered: as an additional host event or by sending separate host and guest invites.

privateNoteTemplate.description: Template for the private note content. Supports variables like {Attendee name}, {Link title}, {Event type title} (legacy), {Location}, {Host name}, {Event duration}, and custom booking field names.

allowAffectingUpcomingBookings.description:
Allows this update to affect upcoming bookings when a live confirmation session exists. Not stored and not returned. `true` confirms the edit:
- Turning seats off cancels every attendee and booking attempt, and new bookings are taken one at a time.
- Turning confirmation off rejects pending requests, leaves accepted attendees, and confirms new booking attempts until the seats are full.
- Setting the seat cap below the seats already accepted keeps existing bookings and their seats, and applies the lower cap to new bookings and later confirmations.
`false` and omitting the field leave the update refused when it would affect upcoming bookings.

locations.description: Locations where the event will take place. If not provided, cal video link will be used as the location. Note: Setting a location to a conferencing app does not install the app - the app must already be installed. Via API, only Google Meet (google-meet), Microsoft Teams (office365-video), and Zoom (zoom) can be installed. Cal Video (cal-video) is installed by default. All other conferencing apps must be connected via the Cal.com web app and are not available for Platform plan customers. You can only set an event type location to an app that has already been installed or connected.

actions.name: delete_event_type
actions.description:
Delete an event type. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

actions.name: get_booking_fields
actions.description:
Get booking fields. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Returns default and custom booking fields, plus any read-only workflow-added fields. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_READ` scope is required.

actions.name: replace_booking_fields
actions.description:
Replace booking fields. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Replaces all booking fields. Omitted custom fields are deleted, while omitted default fields are restored with their default settings. Use `PATCH` to update specific fields. Workflow-added fields are read-only and ignored. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

bookingFields.description: Booking fields to add or use as a replacement. The array cannot be empty, contain duplicate default fields or custom slugs, or use a default field's slug for a custom field. When replacing fields, at least one of `email` or `attendeePhoneNumber` must remain visible and required. Workflow-added fields are read-only and ignored when replacing fields.

actions.name: add_custom_booking_fields
actions.description:
Add custom booking fields. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Adds custom booking fields. Default and workflow-added fields cannot be added through this endpoint. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

bookingFields.description: Booking fields to add or use as a replacement. The array cannot be empty, contain duplicate default fields or custom slugs, or use a default field's slug for a custom field. When replacing fields, at least one of `email` or `attendeePhoneNumber` must remain visible and required. Workflow-added fields are read-only and ignored when replacing fields.

For example, if URL contains query parameter `?name=John%20Doe`,    the first name and last name fields will be prefilled with these values and disabled.    The value may also be a JSON object such as `{"firstName":"John","lastName":"Doe"}`.

actions.name: update_booking_fields
actions.description:
Update booking fields. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Updates the booking fields identified by `slug`. Omitted properties keep their current values. Workflow-added fields are read-only. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

bookingFields.description: Booking fields to update. Identify each field by `slug` and include at least one property to change. `field` and a custom field's `type` cannot be changed. Null values and repeated slugs are not allowed, except `showWhen: null`, which removes a follow-up condition. Workflow-added fields are read-only.

actions.name: delete_custom_booking_field
actions.description:
Delete a custom booking field. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Deletes the custom booking field identified by `slug`. Default fields cannot be deleted, set hidden instead. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

actions.description: Create a webhook. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

payloadTemplate.description: The template of the payload that will be sent to the subscriberUrl, check cal.com/help/webhooks for more information

customHeaders.description: Static HTTP headers sent on every webhook delivery (e.g. Authorization). Max 10 headers, values up to 4 KiB, stored encrypted and redacted on read. Changing `subscriberUrl` drops the stored values unless you send them again. An instance without the webhook header keyring (`CALCOM_KEYRING_WEBHOOK_HEADERS`) answers 400 to any request that sends headers.

name.description: HTTP header name, at most 256 characters. Names starting with `X-Cal-` are reserved for Cal.com's own headers. Blocked names: host, content-length, transfer-encoding, connection, keep-alive, upgrade, trailer, te, proxy-authorization.

value.description: HTTP header value. Omit (or send the redacted `"***"`) on update to keep the stored value, as long as `subscriberUrl` stays the same: stored values are never sent to a new URL. Values are stored encrypted and are always redacted as `"***"` on read.

version.description: The payload format version of the webhook. Version 2026-07-27 adds generated ICS calendar content (`attendeeIcsContent`, `organizerIcsContent`) to BOOKING_CREATED, BOOKING_RESCHEDULED, BOOKING_CANCELLED, BOOKING_SEAT_ACCEPTED, and BOOKING_PAID (when the payment accepted the booking) payloads. Every version's builder-produced payload carries a `payload.platformOAuthClientId` field naming the owning platform OAuth client (`null` for non-platform events; for the flat-delivered MEETING_STARTED/MEETING_ENDED bodies the field appears at the top level of the body). Zapier deliveries, custom payload templates that do not reference the field, the `AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` / `AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` bodies (delivered verbatim from the fire-time blob, never built) and the legacy `FORM_SUBMITTED_NO_EVENT` fallback delivery omit it.

time.description: How long after the booking start time the no-show triggers are evaluated. Required, together with timeUnit, when subscribing to AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW or AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW

timeUnit.description: The unit of the no-show time value

actions.name: list_events_cursor_pagination
actions.description:
List Events (cursor pagination). Returns the Events the authenticated user hosts: Events they own, plus Events they have accepted a co-host invitation to. A co-hosted Event may be owned by a team, so a team-owned Event can appear here — but team-owned Events the user neither hosts nor co-hosts are not returned by this endpoint; list those with `GET /v2/teams/{teamId}/events`. Ordered by start time, newest first when `status` is omitted.

Cursor-based pagination: pass `pagination.nextCursor` from a previous response as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page; omit `cursor` for the first page. `pagination.hasMore` is `false` and `pagination.nextCursor` is `null` on the last page...

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for cursor-based pagination. Pass the `pagination.nextCursor` value from a previous response to fetch the next page. Omit to fetch the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of Events to return.

slug.description: Filter by the event's public page slug (cal.com/{slug}).

status.description: Filter events by lifecycle status. `draft`: not published and not cancelled, ordered soonest first. `upcoming`: published and not yet ended, or cancelled but not yet started, ordered soonest first. `past`: everything else, ordered latest first. Omit to return all statuses, newest first. When provided, `pagination.nextCursor` encodes the status — cursors from one status value cannot be used with another and return 400.

actions.name: create_event
actions.description:
Create an Event. Creates a draft Event for the authenticated user. A draft is not public and nobody can register until it is published with `POST /v2/events/{uuid}/publish`. To create an Event owned by a team, use `POST /v2/teams/{teamId}/events`.

`startTime` and `endTime` are ISO 8601 in UTC; `startTime` must not be in the past and `endTime` must be after `startTime`.

`guestList` controls whether guests see names, a count, or neither. `locations` sets where the Event happens; set `price` and `currency` on a location to charge for that place.

Events are fixed-date RSVP pages served at cal.com/{slug}; they are not event types (bookable meeting templates) or calendar events.

Learn more ...

startTime.description: When the Event starts, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. It must not be in the past.

endTime.description: When the Event ends, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. It must be after `startTime`.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone the Event's times are shown in.

slug.description: Public page slug (cal.com/{slug}): 10-100 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Generated from the title when omitted.

description.description: What the Event is about, shown on its page.

visibility.description: Once published: PUBLIC is listed on the owner's page, UNLISTED only opens from its link. Defaults to PUBLIC.

capacity.description: The most guests the Event can take. Omit or pass null for unlimited. Ignored once any location has its own `capacity`: the Event then takes the sum of the location capacities, or is unlimited if any location has none. The waitlist only opens when the Event or the chosen location is full, so it only works when capacity is set on the Event or on a location.

waitlistEnabled.description: Let guests join a waitlist when the Event is full. The waitlist only opens when the Event or the chosen location is full, so it only works when capacity is set on the Event or on a location.

paymentTimeoutMinutes.description: How many minutes a guest's seat is held while they pay. null uses the default of 10 minutes.

registrationOpensAt.description: When guests can start registering, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Must be before registration closes. null opens registration when the Event is published.

registrationClosesAt.description: When registration closes, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Must not be after `startTime`. null closes registration when the Event starts. Guests already on the waitlist can still be promoted after it closes.

requiresApproval.description: Registrations wait for a host's approval.

showOrganizerEmail.description: Show the organizer's email to guests.

guestList.description: Who guests can see on the Event's page. `names` lists them, `count` shows how many, `hidden` shows neither. Defaults to `names`.

showPresentedBy.description: Show who the Event is presented by.

theme.description: Default theme of the event page. null follows the visitor's system setting.

colors.description: Exactly three hex colors the effect is drawn with.

background.description: Animated background of the event page.

title.description: Heading above the people on the event page.

role.description: Shown under the person's name, e.g. their job title or act.

avatarUrl.description: Avatar for this person. Must be a Cal Event media URL returned by the person avatar endpoint.

media.description: Spotify, YouTube or SoundCloud links, shown as players with the person.

lineup.description: Speakers or performers on the event page. Avatars need the Event uuid, so create people without avatarUrl and upload avatars with the person avatar endpoint afterwards.

schedule.description: Agenda on the event page. Each item has either a startTime or a timeLabel. Avatars need the Event uuid, so create people without avatarUrl and upload avatars with the person avatar endpoint afterwards.

startTime.description: When the item starts, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Send either startTime or timeLabel. Required when endTime is set.

endTime.description: When the item ends, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Must be after startTime.

timeLabel.description: Free text such as "Doors open" for an item without a startTime. Send either startTime or timeLabel.

avatarUrl.description: Avatar for this person. Must be a Cal Event media URL returned by the person avatar endpoint.

hosts.description: The Event's hosts. The creator is always a host and always listed first, even when not passed. Personal Events can only have the creator, so passing other ids returns a 400. On team Events every id must be an accepted team member, otherwise it returns a 400.

liveStreams.description: Links where people can watch the event live.

url.description: Where people can watch the event live.

category.description: What kind of event it is. If not passed, it's guessed from the title.

price.description: Price of the Event, in the currency's smallest unit. Only for Events without locations, which need at least one live stream; Events with locations are priced per location. On update, null makes the Event free. Check `paymentsEnabled` on the Event before setting it.

currency.description: Cal Pay currency code. Required when `price` is set.

locations.description: Where the Event happens. Links can repeat. An Event can have one address and one conferencing location, either an integration or the organizer's default app.

price.description: Price for this location, in the currency's smallest unit.

currency.description: Cal Pay currency code. Required when `price` is set.

capacity.description: Seats at this location. Omit for unlimited. All locations together can have at most 100000 seats.

actions.name: get_event
actions.description: Get an Event. Returns one Event by UUID. The authenticated user must be its owner, one of its hosts, an accepted co-host, or a member of the owning team. PBAC permission for team events: `calEvent.read`. Learn more about API access control at https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/access-control. Events are fixed-date RSVP pages served at cal.com/{slug}; they are not event types (bookable meeting templates) or calendar events. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_READ` scope is required.

uuid.description: Event UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID (e.g. `018ff5cd-6dc4-7d57-bcbc-374702ca8b38`) or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form (e.g. `1cbZYoAFoJdwqN4tixezd5`).

actions.name: update_event
actions.description:
Update an Event. Updates the properties sent and leaves every other property as it is. Takes the same properties as `POST /v2/events` except `locations`, which have their own endpoints under `/v2/events/{uuid}/locations`.

`hosts`, `liveStreams`, `registrationFields`, `lineup` and `schedule` replace the whole stored list. `lineup: null` removes the lineup. Pass `null` to `capacity` for unlimited guests.

The slug and the guest list can't change once the Event is published, and a cancelled Event can't be updated. New times must keep every schedule item inside the Event. An accepted co-host can update the Event but not its hosts, slug or policies such as `visibility`, `guestList` or `requir...

uuid.description: Event UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID (e.g. `018ff5cd-6dc4-7d57-bcbc-374702ca8b38`) or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form (e.g. `1cbZYoAFoJdwqN4tixezd5`).

endTime.description: When the Event ends, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. It must be after `startTime`.

timeZone.description: The IANA time zone the Event's times are shown in.

description.description: What the Event is about, shown on its page.

paymentTimeoutMinutes.description: How many minutes a guest's seat is held while they pay. null uses the default of 10 minutes.

registrationOpensAt.description: When guests can start registering, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Must be before registration closes. null opens registration when the Event is published.

registrationClosesAt.description: When registration closes, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Must not be after `startTime`. null closes registration when the Event starts. Guests already on the waitlist can still be promoted after it closes.

theme.description: Default theme of the event page. null follows the visitor's system setting.

colors.description: Exactly three hex colors the effect is drawn with.

background.description: Animated background of the event page.

title.description: Heading above the people on the event page.

role.description: Shown under the person's name, e.g. their job title or act.

avatarUrl.description: Avatar for this person. Must be a Cal Event media URL returned by the person avatar endpoint.

media.description: Spotify, YouTube or SoundCloud links, shown as players with the person.

lineup.description: Speakers or performers on the event page. Avatars need the Event uuid, so create people without avatarUrl and upload avatars with the person avatar endpoint afterwards.

schedule.description: Agenda on the event page. Each item has either a startTime or a timeLabel. Avatars need the Event uuid, so create people without avatarUrl and upload avatars with the person avatar endpoint afterwards.

startTime.description: When the item starts, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Send either startTime or timeLabel. Required when endTime is set.

endTime.description: When the item ends, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. Must be after startTime.

timeLabel.description: Free text such as "Doors open" for an item without a startTime. Send either startTime or timeLabel.

avatarUrl.description: Avatar for this person. Must be a Cal Event media URL returned by the person avatar endpoint.

registrationFields.description: The questions guests answer when they register. Every guest sees every question, so `showWhen` is rejected.

url.description: Where people can watch the event live.

startTime.description: When the Event starts, in ISO 8601 format in UTC timezone. It must be before `endTime`.

category.description: What kind of event it is.

An upcoming published Event is cancelled first, notifying its guests, and disappears from listings immediately; it is permanently removed once those notices have gone out. An ended Event that still has confirmed guests cannot be deleted, and a published paid Event cannot be deleted because its payment records are retained. The authenticated user must be its owner, one of its hosts, or a member of the owning team; an external co-host gets 404. PBAC permission for team events: `calEvent.delete`. actions.name: publish_event

A free Event approves them in this request and returns `completed` with the counts. A paid Event sends each guest a payment request in the background and returns `started`.         becomes fully booked, a new day (e.g., December 2) will open up to ensure 3 available days are always visible.
        In this mode 'value' must be at most 61, because availability is only searched up to 61 days ahead.
      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the
        moment someone is trying to book. For example, if 'value' is 3, availability is only on Mondays, and the current 
        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

type.description: Whether the window should be business days, calendar days or a range of dates

value.description: How many calendar days into the future can this event be booked

rolling.description:
Determines the behavior of the booking window:
      - If **true**, the window is rolling. This means the number of available days will always be equal the specified 'value' 
        and adjust dynamically as bookings are made. For example, if 'value' is 3 and availability is only on Mondays, 
        a booker attempting to schedule on November 10 will see slots on November 11, 18, and 25. As one of these days 
        becomes fully booked, a new day (e.g., December 2) will open up to ensure 3 available days are always visible.
        In this mode 'value' must be at most 61, because availability is only searched up to 61 days ahead.
      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the
        moment someone is trying to book. For example, if 'value' is 3, availability is only on Mondays, and the current 
        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

As an exception, round robin event types accept `hosts` together with `assignAllTeamMembers: true` to mark specific team members as fixed hosts (entries with `mandatory: true`); non-mandatory entries are silently ignored in that combination because they would be added to the round robin pool by `assignAllTeamMembers` anyway. For round robin event types, `hosts` may be provided alongside `assignAllTeamMembers: true` solely to designate fixed hosts via `mandatory: true` entries.

All other conferencing apps must be connected via the Cal.com web app and are not available for Platform plan customers. You can only set an event type location to an app that has already been installed or connected.

rolling.description:
Determines the behavior of the booking window:
      - If **true**, the window is rolling. This means the number of available days will always be equal the specified 'value' 
        and adjust dynamically as bookings are made. For example, if 'value' is 3 and availability is only on Mondays, 
        a booker attempting to schedule on November 10 will see slots on November 11, 18, and 25. As one of these days 
        becomes fully booked, a new day (e.g., December 2) will open up to ensure 3 available days are always visible.
        In this mode 'value' must be at most 61, because availability is only searched up to 61 days ahead.
      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the
        moment someone is trying to book. For example, if 'value' is 3, availability is only on Mondays, and the current 
        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

Allows this update to affect upcoming bookings when a live confirmation session exists. Not stored and not returned. `true` confirms the edit:
- Turning seats off cancels every attendee and booking attempt, and new bookings are taken one at a time.
- Turning confirmation off rejects pending requests, leaves accepted attendees, and confirms new booking attempts until the seats are full.
- Setting the seat cap below the seats already accepted keeps existing bookings and their seats, and applies the lower cap to new bookings and later confirmations.
`false` and omitting the field leave the update refused when it would affect upcoming bookings.

The scheduling type for the team event - collective or roundRobin. ❗If you change scheduling type you must also provide `hosts` or `assignAllTeamMembers` in the request body, otherwise the event type will have no hosts - this is required because
      in case of collective event type all hosts are mandatory but in case of round robin some or non can be mandatory so we can't predict how you want the hosts to be setup which is why you must provide that information.  If you want to convert round robin or collective into managed or managed into round robin or collective then you will have to create a new team event type and delete old one.

actions.name: delete_team_event_type_in_organization
actions.description:
Delete an organization team event type. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Required membership role: `team admin`. PBAC permission: `eventType.delete`. Learn more about API access control at https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/access-control. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

teamId.description: The team's uuid (preferred), its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, or its numeric id.

actions.name: get_organization_team_event_type_calendar_invite_templates
actions.description: Get organization team event-type calendar-invite templates. Returns host and guest settings resolved from the event type, organization default, then Cal.com's standard description. Access matches reading the team event type: the `eventType.readTeamEventTypes` PBAC permission, or team ADMIN/OWNER role when PBAC does not grant it. OAuth clients require `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_READ`. Custom templates are limited to 5,000 characters. A team-scope mismatch returns 404. Managed children inherit their parent's settings and are marked read-only.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

teamId.description: The team's uuid (preferred), its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, or its numeric id.

actions.name: update_organization_team_event_type_calendar_invite_templates
actions.description: Update organization team event-type calendar-invite templates. Updates one or both audiences without changing other event-type fields; omitted audiences remain unchanged. Access matches updating the team event type: the `eventType.update` PBAC permission, or team ADMIN/OWNER role when PBAC does not grant it. OAuth clients require `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_WRITE`. Custom templates are limited to 5,000 characters; HTML tags are stripped and Markdown links are kept. Managed children are read-only and return HTTP 400. A team-scope mismatch returns 404.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

teamId.description: The team's uuid (preferred), its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, or its numeric id.

mode.description: Template source. `inherit` uses the organization default, `standard` uses Cal.com's standard description, and `custom` uses this object's template.

template.description: Custom Markdown description. Required only when mode is custom; maximum length is 5000 characters.

actions.name: retrieve_team_event_types
actions.description:
Get all team event types. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Use the optional `sortCreatedAt` query parameter to order results by creation date (by ID). Accepts "asc" (oldest first) or "desc" (newest first). When not provided, no explicit ordering is applied. Required membership role: `org admin`. PBAC permission: `eventType.readOrgEventTypes`. Learn more about API access control at https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/access-control. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `ORG_EVENT_TYPE_READ` scope is required.

actions.name: add_custom_organization_team_booking_fields
actions.description:
Add custom organization team booking fields. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Adds custom booking fields. Default and workflow-added fields cannot be added through this endpoint. Required membership role: `team admin`. PBAC permission: `eventType.update`. Learn more about API access control at https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/access-control. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

teamId.description: The team's uuid (preferred), its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, or its numeric id.

bookingFields.description: Booking fields to add or use as a replacement. The array cannot be empty, contain duplicate default fields or custom slugs, or use a default field's slug for a custom field. When replacing fields, at least one of `email` or `attendeePhoneNumber` must remain visible and required. Workflow-added fields are read-only and ignored when replacing fields.

field.description: Only allowed value is 'name'.

slug.description: Only allowed value is 'name'.

variant.description: Only allowed value is 'fullName'. Used for having a single booking field for the attendee's full name.

disableOnPrefill.description: Disable this booking field if the URL contains query parameter with key equal to the slug and prefill it with the provided value.    For example, if URL contains query parameter `&name=bob`,    the name field will be prefilled with this value and disabled.

field.description: Only allowed value is 'name'.

variant.description: Only allowed value is 'splitName'. Used to have 2 booking fields — one for first name and one for last name.

lastNameRequired.description: Whether the last name sub-field is required. The first name sub-field is always required and cannot be configured.

disableOnPrefill.description: Disable this booking field if the URL contains query parameter with key equal to the slug and prefill it with the provided value.    For example, if URL contains query parameter `?name=John%20Doe`,    the first name and last name fields will be prefilled with these values and disabled.    The value may also be a JSON object such as `{"firstName":"John","lastName":"Doe"}`.

actions.description:
Get available time slots for an event type. There are 4 ways to get available slots for event type of an individual user:

      1. By event type id. Example '/v2/slots?eventTypeId=10&start=2033-09-05&end=2033-09-06&timeZone=Europe/Rome'

      2. By event type slug + username. Example '/v2/slots?eventTypeSlug=intro&username=bob&start=2033-09-05&end=2033-09-06'

      3. By event type slug + username + organization slug when searching within an organization. Example '/v2/slots?organizationSlug=org-slug&eventTypeSlug=intro&username=bob&start=2033-09-05&end=2033-09-06'

      4. By usernames only (used for dynamic event type - there is no specific event but you want to know when 2 or more p...

hostUsernames.description:
Only for collective event types: returns the slots when just these hosts are all available, instead of every host. Pass usernames separated by commas e.g. ?hostUsernames=alice,bob, or repeat the key e.g. ?hostUsernames=alice&hostUsernames=bob. For a team in an organization, use the hosts' organization usernames.

      Every username must be a host of the event type, otherwise the request fails with 400 and the message "invalid_hosts". At most 50 distinct usernames of at most 255 characters each. Leaving it out, or passing it empty, returns the slots of every host. A seated event type refuses it with 400.

      Ignored for other event types, for dynamic events (usernames) and when bookingUidToReschedule is passed: a reschedule keeps the hosts of the original booking. To book the slot with the same hosts, pass the same hostUsernames when creating the booking.

start.description:

end.description:

rolling.description:
Determines the behavior of the booking window:
      - If **true**, the window is rolling. This means the number of available days will always be equal the specified 'value' 
        and adjust dynamically as bookings are made. For example, if 'value' is 3 and availability is only on Mondays, 
        a booker attempting to schedule on November 10 will see slots on November 11, 18, and 25. As one of these days 
        becomes fully booked, a new day (e.g., December 2) will open up to ensure 3 available days are always visible.
        In this mode 'value' must be at most 61, because availability is only searched up to 61 days ahead.
      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the
        moment someone is trying to book. For example, if 'value' is 3, availability is only on Mondays, and the current 
        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

        becomes fully booked, a new day (e.g., December 2) will open up to ensure 3 available days are always visible.

      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the
        moment someone is trying to book. For example, if 'value' is 3, availability is only on Mondays, and the current 
        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

As an exception, round robin event types accept `hosts` together with `assignAllTeamMembers: true` to mark specific team members as fixed hosts (entries with `mandatory: true`); non-mandatory entries are silently ignored in that combination because they would be added to the round robin pool by `assignAllTeamMembers` anyway. assignAllTeamMembers.description: If true, all current and future team members will be assigned to this event type. Mutually exclusive with `hosts` for collective and managed event types. For round robin event types, `hosts` may be provided alongside `assignAllTeamMembers: true` solely to designate fixed hosts via `mandatory: true` entries.

All other conferencing apps must be connected via the Cal.com web app and are not available for Platform plan customers. You can only set an event type location to an app that has already been installed or connected.

rolling.description:
Determines the behavior of the booking window:
      - If **true**, the window is rolling. This means the number of available days will always be equal the specified 'value' 
        and adjust dynamically as bookings are made. For example, if 'value' is 3 and availability is only on Mondays, 
        a booker attempting to schedule on November 10 will see slots on November 11, 18, and 25. As one of these days 
        becomes fully booked, a new day (e.g., December 2) will open up to ensure 3 available days are always visible.
        In this mode 'value' must be at most 61, because availability is only searched up to 61 days ahead.
      - If **false**, the window is fixed. This means the booking window only considers the next 'value' days from the
        moment someone is trying to book. For example, if 'value' is 3, availability is only on Mondays, and the current 
        date is November 10, the booker will only see slots on November 11 because the window is restricted to the next 
        3 calendar days (November 10–12).

allowAffectingUpcomingBookings.description:
Allows this update to affect upcoming bookings when a live confirmation session exists. Not stored and not returned. `true` confirms the edit:
- Turning seats off cancels every attendee and booking attempt, and new bookings are taken one at a time.
- Turning confirmation off rejects pending requests, leaves accepted attendees, and confirms new booking attempts until the seats are full.
- Setting the seat cap below the seats already accepted keeps existing bookings and their seats, and applies the lower cap to new bookings and later confirmations.
`false` and omitting the field leave the update refused when it would affect upcoming bookings.

schedulingType.description:
The scheduling type for the team event - collective or roundRobin. ❗If you change scheduling type you must also provide `hosts` or `assignAllTeamMembers` in the request body, otherwise the event type will have no hosts - this is required because
      in case of collective event type all hosts are mandatory but in case of round robin some or non can be mandatory so we can't predict how you want the hosts to be setup which is why you must provide that information.  If you want to convert round robin or collective into managed or managed into round robin or collective then you will have to create a new team event type and delete old one.

hosts.description: Hosts contain specific team members you want to assign to this event type. To assign every current and future team member use `assignAllTeamMembers: true` and omit this field. As an exception, round robin event types accept `hosts` together with `assignAllTeamMembers: true` to mark specific team members as fixed hosts (entries with `mandatory: true`); non-mandatory entries are silently ignored in that combination because they would be added to the round robin pool by `assignAllTeamMembers` anyway. For platform customers the hosts can include userIds only of managed users.

userId.description: Which user is the host of this event

mandatory.description: Only relevant for round robin event types. If true then the user must attend the round robin event always (fixed host). This may be combined with `assignAllTeamMembers: true` on round robin event types — entries marked `mandatory: true` become fixed hosts while every other team member fills the round robin pool.

weight.description: Only relevant for round robin event types with `isRRWeightsEnabled: true`. Relative share of bookings this host receives - a host with weight 200 gets twice as many bookings as a host with weight 100. Defaults to 100.

assignAllTeamMembers.description: If true, all current and future team members will be assigned to this event type. Mutually exclusive with `hosts` for collective and managed event types. For round robin event types, `hosts` may be provided alongside `assignAllTeamMembers: true` solely to designate fixed hosts via `mandatory: true` entries.

locations.description: Locations where the event will take place. If not provided, cal video link will be used as the location. Note: Setting a location to a conferencing app does not install the app - the app must already be installed. Via API, only Google Meet (google-meet), Microsoft Teams (office365-video), and Zoom (zoom) can be installed. Cal Video (cal-video) is installed by default. All other conferencing apps must be connected via the Cal.com web app and are not available for Platform plan customers. You can only set an event type location to an app that has already been installed or connected.

actions.name: delete_event_type_in_team
actions.description:
Delete a team event type. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Required membership role: `team admin`. PBAC permission: `eventType.delete`. Learn more about API access control at https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/access-control. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

teamId.description: The team's uuid (preferred), its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, or its numeric id.

actions.name: get_team_event_type_calendar_invite_templates
actions.description: Get team event-type calendar-invite templates. Returns host and guest settings resolved from the event type, an organization default when available, then Cal.com's standard description. Access matches reading the team event type: the `eventType.readTeamEventTypes` PBAC permission, or team ADMIN/OWNER role when PBAC does not grant it. OAuth clients require `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_READ`. Custom templates are limited to 5,000 characters. Event types outside the requested team return 404. Managed children inherit their parent's settings and are marked read-only.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

teamId.description: The team's uuid (preferred), its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, or its numeric id.

actions.name: update_team_event_type_calendar_invite_templates
actions.description: Update team event-type calendar-invite templates. Updates one or both audiences without changing other event-type fields; omitted audiences remain unchanged. Access matches updating the team event type: the `eventType.update` PBAC permission, or team ADMIN/OWNER role when PBAC does not grant it. OAuth clients require `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_WRITE`. Custom templates are limited to 5,000 characters; HTML tags are stripped and Markdown links are kept. Managed children are read-only and return HTTP 400. Event types outside the requested team return 404.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

teamId.description: The team's uuid (preferred), its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, or its numeric id.

mode.description: Template source. `inherit` uses the organization default, `standard` uses Cal.com's standard description, and `custom` uses this object's template.

template.description: Custom Markdown description. Required only when mode is custom; maximum length is 5000 characters.

actions.name: add_custom_team_booking_fields
actions.description:
Add custom team booking fields. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Adds custom booking fields. Default and workflow-added fields cannot be added through this endpoint. Required membership role: `team admin`. PBAC permission: `eventType.update`. Learn more about API access control at https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/access-control. If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `TEAM_EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.

eventTypeId.description: Numeric event type ID or its UUID. Accepts the canonical UUID or its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, e.g. the one in an app.cal.com/links/{uuid} URL.

teamId.description: The team's uuid (preferred), its short-uuid (Flickr Base58) form, or its numeric id.

bookingFields.description: Booking fields to add or use as a replacement. The array cannot be empty, contain duplicate default fields or custom slugs, or use a default field's slug for a custom field. When replacing fields, at least one of `email` or `attendeePhoneNumber` must remain visible and required. Workflow-added fields are read-only and ignored when replacing fields.

field.description: Only allowed value is 'name'.

slug.description: Only allowed value is 'name'.

variant.description: Only allowed value is 'fullName'. Used for having a single booking field for the attendee's full name.

disableOnPrefill.description: Disable this booking field if the URL contains query parameter with key equal to the slug and prefill it with the provided value.    For example, if URL contains query parameter `&name=bob`,    the name field will be prefilled with this value and disabled.

field.description: Only allowed value is 'name'.

slug.description: Only allowed value is 'name'.

variant.description: Only allowed value is 'splitName'. Used to have 2 booking fields — one for first name and one for last name.

lastNameRequired.description: Whether the last name sub-field is required. The first name sub-field is always required and cannot be configured.

disableOnPrefill.description: Disable this booking field if the URL contains query parameter with key equal to the slug and prefill it with the provided value.    For example, if URL contains query parameter `?name=John%20Doe`,    the first name and last name fields will be prefilled with these values and disabled.    The value may also be a JSON object such as `{"firstName":"John","lastName":"Doe"}`.

actions.name: update_team_booking_fields
actions.description:
Update team booking fields. <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>

Updates the booking fields identified by `slug`. Omitted properties keep their current values. Workflow-added fields are read-only. Required membership role: `team admin`. actions.description: Create routing form response and get available slots. Only available for teams that are not part of an organization - for a team within an organization use the organization team endpoint instead. Required membership role: `team member`. PBAC permission: `routingForm.create`. Learn more about API access control at https://cal.com/docs/api-reference/v2/access-control. start.description:
Time starting from which available slots should be checked.
    
      Must be in UTC timezone as ISO 8601 datestring.
      
      You can pass date without hours which defaults to start of day or specify hours:
      2024-08-13 (will have hours 00:00:00 aka at very beginning of the date) or you can specify hours manually like 2024-08-13T09:00:00Z

end.description:
Time until which available slots should be checked.
      
      Must be in UTC timezone as ISO 8601 datestring.
      
      You can pass date without hours which defaults to end of day or specify hours:
      2024-08-20 (will have hours 23:59:59 aka at the very end of the date) or you can specify hours manually like 2024-08-20T18:00:00Z

timeZone.description: Time zone in which the available slots should be returned. Defaults to UTC.

duration.description: If event type has multiple possible durations then you can specify the desired duration here. Also, if you are fetching slots for a dynamic event then you can specify the duration her which defaults to 30, meaning that returned slots will be each 30 minutes long.

format.description: Format of slot times in response. Use 'range' to get start and end times.

bookingUidToReschedule.description: The unique identifier of the booking being rescheduled. When provided will ensure that the original booking time appears within the returned available slots when rescheduling.

rescheduleWithSameHost.description: Only for round robin event types that allow the person rescheduling to choose the host. True returns slots of the original host, false returns slots of any available host. Ignored for other event types.

queueResponse.description: Whether to queue the form response.

actions.name: get_all_timezones
actions.description:
Get timezones. Returns the cities Cal.com knows a timezone for, as a `city` to show the user and the IANA `timezone` to store and to send back to Cal.com. Without `search` every city is returned, around 7000 of them.

`search` searches the full source dataset by city name and additionally matches timezone names, so a search for an abbreviation such as `PDT` resolves to `{ "city": "Pacific Time - US & Canada", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles" }`. City and alias names match by case-insensitive substring; complete IANA identifiers also match by case-insensitive equality. Partial IANA identifiers are not matched; timezone matches come first, then cities ordered by population, so the most lik...

search.description: Match city or timezone names by case-insensitive substring, or a complete IANA timezone identifier by case-insensitive equality. Omit it to get every city.

limit.description: Return at most this many entries (a whole number from 1 to 250). Results are ordered by relevance, so a limit keeps the entries a user is most likely to want. Omit it to get every match.
