payloadTemplate.description: The template of the payload that will be sent to the subscriberUrl, check cal.com/help/webhooks for more information

customHeaders.description: Static HTTP headers sent on every webhook delivery (e.g. Authorization). Max 10 headers, values up to 4 KiB, stored encrypted and redacted on read. Changing `subscriberUrl` drops the stored values unless you send them again. An instance without the webhook header keyring (`CALCOM_KEYRING_WEBHOOK_HEADERS`) answers 400 to any request that sends headers.

name.description: HTTP header name, at most 256 characters. Names starting with `X-Cal-` are reserved for Cal.com's own headers. Blocked names: host, content-length, transfer-encoding, connection, keep-alive, upgrade, trailer, te, proxy-authorization.

value.description: HTTP header value. Omit (or send the redacted `"***"`) on update to keep the stored value, as long as `subscriberUrl` stays the same: stored values are never sent to a new URL. Values are stored encrypted and are always redacted as `"***"` on read.

version.description: The payload format version of the webhook. Version 2026-07-27 adds generated ICS calendar content (`attendeeIcsContent`, `organizerIcsContent`) to BOOKING_CREATED, BOOKING_RESCHEDULED, BOOKING_CANCELLED, BOOKING_SEAT_ACCEPTED, and BOOKING_PAID (when the payment accepted the booking) payloads. Every version's builder-produced payload carries a `payload.platformOAuthClientId` field naming the owning platform OAuth client (`null` for non-platform events; for the flat-delivered MEETING_STARTED/MEETING_ENDED bodies the field appears at the top level of the body). Zapier deliveries, custom payload templates that do not reference the field, the `AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` / `AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` bodies (delivered verbatim from the fire-time blob, never built) and the legacy `FORM_SUBMITTED_NO_EVENT` fallback delivery omit it.

time.description: How long after the booking start time the no-show triggers are evaluated. Required, together with timeUnit, when subscribing to AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW or AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW

timeUnit.description: The unit of the no-show time value

action.description: Marks the step that splits the workflow into conditional paths. It is always placed after every step outside a path, followed by the steps inside its paths, so it takes no stepNumber. Send `paths` to author the split and omit this step to delete it.

paths.description: The branches this step splits into, in the order they should appear on the canvas. A split needs at least two. Omit to leave the persisted branches untouched.

matches.description: How conditions must match: all (every condition), any (at least one), none (no conditions), or not_all (at least one condition does not match). Omit to preserve an existing branch’s mode; new branches default to all.

conditions.description: The conditions deciding whether this branch matches. Omit or send an empty list for a branch that always matches.

items.description: an object (see the provider's API docs)

pathId.description: Id of the filter path this split itself sits inside. Omit it for a split at the top level.

matches.description: all: every condition matches; any: at least one matches; none: no conditions match; not_all: at least one condition does not match.

conditions.description: The conditions every following step is gated on. Omit to leave the persisted conditions untouched; send an empty list for a gate that passes everything.

field.description: The booking question or event field this condition reads. Use a field identifier returned by the workflow condition-fields endpoint.

pathId.description: Id of the conditional path this filter itself sits inside. Omit it for a filter at the top level.

action.description: Marks an existing delay step. Delays can only be created or edited in the Cal.com app. When updating steps, include this step as { action: "delay", id } using the id returned by GET so the wait is preserved. Its position is fixed, so it takes no stepNumber: an update that moves another step to the other side of it, or reuses the stepNumber GET returned for it, is rejected.

id.description: Unique identifier of the existing delay step. A delay step cannot be created through the API, so the id is required.

action.description: Marks the step that looks the attendee up with the lead enrichment provider before the steps after it run. It can only be added or configured in the Cal.com app. When updating steps, include this step as { action: "lead_enrichment", id } using the id returned by GET so the lookup is preserved. Its position is fixed, so it takes no stepNumber: an update that moves another step to the other side of it, or reuses the stepNumber GET returned for it, is rejected.

id.description: Unique identifier of the existing lead enrichment step. A lead enrichment step cannot be created through the API, so the id is required.

action.description: Action to perform

stepNumber.description: Step number in the workflow sequence

id.description: Workflow step id. Omit it when creating a new webhook step.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL that receives signed booking payloads. Omission keeps the saved URL.

secret.description: HMAC key for X-Cal-Signature-256. Omission keeps the saved secret, null removes it, and a string replaces it. This secret is write-only and is never returned.

pathId.description: Id of the conditional path this step belongs to, so it only runs when that path's conditions match. It must name a path defined in this request or already persisted on an echoed gate. Omit it for a step that always runs.

actions.name: delete_workflow
actions.description: Delete your workflow. Delete an event-type workflow owned by the authenticated user. Not available to third-party OAuth access tokens.

actions.name: get_fields_workflow_s_conditions_can_read
actions.description: Get the fields a workflow's conditions can read. List the fields a conditional path on this workflow can be written against, with the comparisons each one accepts and how both read in the Cal.com app. The catalog comes from what the workflow is active on — booking questions on its active event types — so it also reports the entities that do not ask for a field. Not available to third-party OAuth access tokens.
